column6: How long does a member have to file an internal appeal after a claim denial, and how quickly will MeridianHealth respond?","The member must file an internal appeal within 180 calendar days of receiving the adverse benefit determination notice. MeridianHealth's decision timeframe is 30 calendar days for pre-service claims, 60 calendar days for post-service claims, and 72 hours for urgent care claims. The appeal is reviewed by a physician not involved in the original decision, and the member may submit additional documentation.","7.1 Internal Appeal

Only Gold and Platinum plans cover infertility treatment, up to 3 IVF cycles per lifetime with a $30,000 lifetime maximum, and prior authorization is required. Diagnostic infertility testing, however, is covered under all plan tiers. Note that state mandates may require additional coverage beyond what's described here.","[EXC-3.1]

Infertility Treatment. IVF, IUI, GIFT, ZIFT, donor procurement, and surrogacy costs excluded under Bronze and Silver plans. State mandates may require additional coverage."

What is the annual out-of-pocket maximum for a family on the Gold 80 plan?,"The annual out-of-pocket maximum for a family on the Gold 80 plan is $13,600 (in-network). This is below the federal ACA ceiling of $21,200 for family coverage in Plan Year 2026.","

column1: Can a member get cosmetic rhinoplasty covered under any MeridianHealth plan?,"No. Cosmetic rhinoplasty is permanently excluded under all MeridianHealth plans, since cosmetic surgery performed primarily to improve appearance (rather than restore function or treat a medical condition) is not covered. The exceptions are reconstructive surgery following a covered accident, injury, or mastectomy — covered under all ACA plans per the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act — and reconstructive surgery for congenital anomalies in dependents under 19, which is also covered. Cosmetic rhinoplasty itself does not fall under either exception.","[EXC-2.1]

Cosmetic Surgery and Procedures. Surgery or procedures performed primarily to improve appearance rather than restore function or treat a medical condition. Includes rhinoplasty for cosmetic purposes, blepharoplasty when not affecting vision, liposuction, abdominoplasty, breast augmentation for cosmetic purposes, hair transplantation, dermabrasion, and chemical peels. EXCEPTION: Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident, injury, or mastectomy is covered under all ACA plans per the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act. Reconstructive surgery for congenital anomalies in dependents under 19 is also covered."

What is the maximum enrollment waiting period for a new employee joining an employer-sponsored group plan?,"The maximum enrollment waiting period for employer-sponsored group plans is 90 calendar days from the employee's date of hire. The employer selects the exact length (0, 30, 60, or 90 days) at group plan setup. Coverage becomes effective on the first day of the month following completion of the waiting period — for example, an employee hired March 15 completes the 90-day wait on June 12, with coverage effective July 1. This is an enrollment waiting period, not a condition-specific exclusion; once coverage begins, all benefits including those for pre-existing conditions are available with no further waiting.","2.2 Employer-Sponsored Group Plans

Employees working 30 or more hours per week are eligible. The employer may impose an enrollment waiting period of up to 90 calendar days from the date of hire. Coverage is effective on the first day of the month following completion of the waiting period. Example: employee hired March 15 completes 90-day wait on June 12; coverage effective July 1. <> 4.2 Employer-Sponsored Plans — Enrollment Waiting Period

Employer-sponsored group plans may include an enrollment waiting period of up to 90 calendar days from the employee's date of hire, as permitted under ACA Section 2708. This is an enrollment waiting period, not a condition-specific exclusion. Once coverage becomes effective, all benefits including those for pre-existing conditions are available with no further waiting. The employer selects the length (0, 30, 60, or 90 days) at group plan setup."

A Supplemental Shield member had cancer diagnosed 10 months before enrollment. Are cancer-related hospitalizations covered under the Supplemental Shield?,"No, not yet. Cancer diagnosed 10 months before the policy's effective date falls within the Supplemental Shield plan's 12-month look-back period, making it a pre-existing condition (cancer, whether active or in remission within 12 months, is explicitly listed as a commonly identified pre-existing condition). The Supplemental Shield plan excludes claims related to pre-existing conditions during the first 12 months from the policy effective date, so cancer-related hospital confinement claims would not be payable until that 12-month period expires. This look-back and exclusion applies specifically to the Supplemental Shield plan; it does not apply to ACA-compliant plans, which cover pre-existing conditions from day one.","The Supplemental Shield plan excludes claims related to pre-existing conditions during the first 12 months from the policy effective date. A pre-existing condition is any condition for which medical advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment was recommended or received during the 12-month look-back period preceding the effective date. After 12 months, pre-existing conditions are eligible on the same basis as any other condition. This exclusion does NOT apply to ACA-compliant plans, which cover pre-existing conditions from day one per the ACA. <> Commonly identified conditions: diabetes (Type 1 and 2), hypertension, asthma/COPD, coronary artery disease, cancer (active or in remission within 12 months), chronic kidney disease, HIV/AIDS, epilepsy, rheumatoid arthritis, and major depressive disorder. This list is not exhaustive. <> Pre-Existing Conditions: 12-month waiting period. Claims related to any condition for which medical advice, diagnosis, care, or treatment was recommended or received during the 12 months immediately preceding the policy effective date are not payable during the first 12 months. After the 12-month period expires, pre-existing conditions are covered under the same terms as any other eligible condition. The look-back applies separately to each covered individual."

What documents are required to file a Supplemental Shield claim?,"To file a Supplemental Shield claim, the member needs: (1) completed Form MH-SS-300, (2) an Attending Physician's Certificate confirming diagnosis, date of onset, and treatment dates, (3) original itemized bills and a discharge summary, and (4) for Critical Illness claims specifically, pathology reports or diagnostic confirmation. Per the documentation checklist, a copy of the MeridianHealth Member ID Card and a copy of government-issued photo ID are also required for all Supplemental Shield claims, along with an Accident/Incident Report if the claim is accident-related and a Coordination of Benefits Statement if the member has dual coverage. Prior authorization approval is not applicable to Supplemental Shield claims.","STEP 1
Complete Form MH-SS-300 (available at www.meridianhealth.example.com/forms). <> STEP 2
Attach Attending Physician's Certificate confirming diagnosis, date of onset, and treatment dates. <> STEP 3
Attach original itemized bills and discharge summary. For Critical Illness claims: pathology reports or diagnostic confirmation. <>

column6: How is the out-of-network reimbursement amount calculated for a Silver 70 plan member?","For a Silver 70 out-of-network claim, MeridianHealth: (1) determines the Maximum Allowable Amount (MAA), which is 150% of the Medicare fee schedule rate for the same service in the same geographic area; (2) applies the out-of-network deductible, which is 2x the in-network deductible for the member's tier ($9,000 for Silver 70, tracked separately from the in-network deductible); (3) applies 50% OON coinsurance, so MeridianHealth pays 50% of the MAA remaining after the deductible and the member pays the other 50%; and (4) treats any provider charge above the MAA as the member's responsibility through balance billing, which does not count toward the deductible or out-of-pocket maximum. For example, on a $5,000 billed OON procedure with a $2,000 Medicare rate, the MAA is $3,000; if the $9,000 OON deductible is unmet, the full $3,000 MAA goes toward the deductible, and the member pays $3,000 (deductible) plus the $2,000 balance-billed excess over the MAA, for $5,000 total, with only the $3,000 counting toward the OON deductible and out-of-pocket maximum.","Reimbursement Calculation (Out-of-Network)

column1: Step 1: Determine the Maximum Allowable Amount (MAA) = 150% of Medicare fee schedule rate for the same service in the same geographic area.
Step 2: Apply the out-of-network deductible (2x the in-network deductible for the member's tier). In-network and OON deductibles are tracked separately.
Step 3: Apply 50% OON coinsurance. MeridianHealth pays 50% of MAA remaining after deductible; member pays 50%.

Step 4: Any charges exceeding MAA = member responsibility (balance billing). Excess charges do NOT count toward deductible or OOP max. <> Example: Silver 70 member, OON procedure billed at $5,000. Medicare rate = $2,000, so MAA = $3,000. OON deductible = $9,000 (2x $4,500). Assuming deductible unmet: full $3,000 MAA applies to deductible. Member pays $3,000 (deductible) + $2,000 (balance bill) = $5,000. Only $3,000 counts toward OON deductible and OOP max. <> Maximum Allowable Amount (MAA). For out-of-network services: 150% of the Medicare fee schedule rate for the same or similar service in the same geographic area. Charges exceeding the MAA are the member's responsibility and do not apply toward deductible or out-of-pocket maximum."

Are hearing aids covered under the Silver plan, and what are the limits?,"Yes. The Silver plan covers one hearing aid per ear every 36 months, up to a maximum of $2,500 per ear. Hearing aids are excluded under the Bronze plan and under the Supplemental Shield plan. Cochlear implants, however, are covered as a surgical benefit under all ACA-compliant plans regardless of tier.","[EXC-3.6]

Hearing Aids. Excluded under Bronze. Silver/Gold/Platinum: 1 per ear every 36 months, max $2,500/ear. Supplemental Shield: excluded. Cochlear implants covered as surgical benefit under all ACA plans. <>
PA = Prior Authorization. Visit/day limits reset January 1. Lifetime limits do not reset."

What preventive care services are covered at zero cost-sharing?,"Preventive care services recommended by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) with a rating of A or B are covered at 100% with no cost-sharing when received from an in-network provider, including annual wellness exams, immunizations, and cancer screenings. Preventive medications on the ACA preventive drug list are also covered at $0 cost-sharing.","Preventive and Wellness Services. Preventive care services recommended by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) with a rating of A or B are covered at 100% with no cost-sharing when received from an in-network provider. This includes annual wellness exams, immunizations, and cancer screenings. <> Prescription Drugs. MeridianHealth uses a four-tier formulary: Tier 1 (generic) — $10 copay; Tier 2 (preferred brand) — $35 copay; Tier 3 (non-preferred brand) — $70 copay; Tier 4 (specialty) — 30% coinsurance up to $300 per fill. Preventive medications on the ACA preventive drug list are covered at $0 cost-sharing."

Does an MRI require prior authorization under MeridianHealth plans?,"Yes. MRI falls under advanced imaging, which is on the list of services requiring prior authorization before being rendered — along with inpatient admissions (except emergency), outpatient surgery over $2,500, CT and PET scans, Tier 4 specialty medications, infertility treatments, bariatric surgery, residential treatment, and DME over $1,000. The member/provider submits Form MH-PA-100 with clinical documentation, and MeridianHealth responds within 5 business days for standard requests or 72 hours for urgent requests. Failure to obtain required prior authorization may result in a 30% reduction in benefits.","Prior Authorization. Advance approval from MeridianHealth's Utilization Management department. Failure to obtain required prior authorization may result in a 30% reduction in benefits. Emergency admissions require notification within 48 hours. <> STEP 2 — Obtain prior authorization

Certain services require prior authorization before being rendered. The PA list is at www.meridianhealth.example.com/prior-auth and includes: inpatient admissions (except emergency), outpatient surgery >$2,500, advanced imaging (MRI, CT, PET), Tier 4 specialty medications, infertility treatments, bariatric surgery, residential treatment, and DME >$1,000. Submit Form MH-PA-100 with clinical documentation. Response: 5 business days standard, 72 hours urgent."

How does the family deductible work — can one family member satisfy the entire family deductible on their own?,"The family deductible is aggregate, meaning covered expenses from any combination of family members count toward it, and it can be satisfied by one member alone or by several members together. However, no single individual pays more than the individual deductible amount. For example, on the Silver 70 plan the family deductible is $9,000 while the individual deductible is $4,500 — so no one family member pays more than $4,500, but the family's combined spending must reach $9,000 before the family deductible is fully satisfied.","Deductible. The amount the member must pay out of pocket for covered services in a plan year before MeridianHealth begins paying its share. The deductible resets on January 1 of each plan year. Family deductible is aggregate — no single individual pays more than the individual deductible amount. <>

column7: What is the grace period for premium payments for members receiving an Advance Premium Tax Credit?","Members receiving an Advance Premium Tax Credit (APTC) get a 90-day grace period for premium payment, per 45 CFR 156.270 (compared with the standard 31-day grace period for other members). During the first 30 days of the grace period, MeridianHealth continues to pay claims; during days 31 through 90, claims may be held pending. If the premium is not paid by the end of the grace period, coverage terminates retroactively to the last day of the last month for which premiums were fully paid.","SECTION 3 — PREMIUM PAYMENT AND GRACE PERIOD

column1: Premiums are due on the first day of each month. MeridianHealth provides a 31-day grace period for premium payment. Members receiving an Advance Premium Tax Credit (APTC) are entitled to a 90-day grace period per 45 CFR 156.270. During the first 30 days, MeridianHealth will continue to pay claims. During days 31 through 90, claims may be held pending. If premiums are not paid by end of grace period, coverage terminates retroactively to the last day of the last month for which premiums were fully paid."

The same exception also covers reconstructive surgery following a covered accident or injury, and reconstructive surgery for congenital anomalies in dependents under age 19.","[EXC-2.1]

EXCEPTION: Reconstructive surgery following a covered accident, injury, or mastectomy is covered under all ACA plans per the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act. What conditions are covered under the Critical Illness Lump Sum benefit of the Supplemental Shield plan?,"The Critical Illness Lump Sum benefit covers first diagnosis of: cancer (invasive), heart attack, stroke, major organ transplant, kidney failure (end-stage renal disease), and coronary artery bypass graft. The lump sum amount is $10,000, $25,000, or $50,000 depending on the option selected at enrollment. Conditions diagnosed within the first 90 days of the policy effective date are not eligible, and a recurrence or new diagnosis of the same condition requires a 12-month separation period from the prior claim.","Critical Illness covered conditions: cancer (invasive), heart attack, stroke, major organ transplant, kidney failure (end-stage renal disease), and coronary artery bypass graft. Conditions diagnosed within the first 90 days of the policy effective date are not eligible. Recurrence or new diagnosis of the same condition requires a 12-month separation period from the prior claim. <>

column4: Can a dependent child aged 24 who is not a student be covered under a parent's MeridianHealth individual plan?","Yes. Dependents are eligible for coverage up to age 26 regardless of student status, marital status, or financial dependency, so a 24-year-old non-student child qualifies as an eligible dependent under a parent's individual or family plan.","2.1 Individual and Family Plans

column1: Any individual residing in a MeridianHealth licensed state who is not incarcerated and is a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or lawfully present in the United States is eligible to enroll during the annual Open Enrollment Period or a qualifying Special Enrollment Period. Dependents eligible for coverage include the member's legal spouse or domestic partner and children up to age 26 regardless of student status, marital status, or financial dependency."

What is the coinsurance rate after deductible for the Silver 70 plan?,"The coinsurance rate after deductible for the Silver 70 plan is 30%. Coinsurance is the percentage of costs for a covered service that the member pays after the annual deductible has been satisfied — so once the Silver 70 deductible is met, MeridianHealth pays the remaining share and the member pays 30% of covered in-network costs.","Coinsurance. The percentage of costs of a covered service that the member pays after the annual deductible has been satisfied. The member's coinsurance percentage varies by plan tier and is specified in the Plan Benefits and Coverage Guide (Document MH-BRO-2026-047). <>

column7: If a member's internal appeal is denied, what is the next step and how long do they have to pursue it?","If the internal appeal is denied, the member may request an external review by a certified Independent Review Organization (IRO) within 4 months. This review is conducted under federal standards (45 CFR Part 147), and the IRO's decision is binding on MeridianHealth. Standard external review decisions take 45 calendar days; expedited reviews take 72 hours. There is no cost to the member for external review.","7.2 External Review

column1: If internal appeal denied, the member may request external review by a certified Independent Review Organization (IRO) within 4 months. Conducted under federal standards (45 CFR Part 147). IRO decision is binding on MeridianHealth. Standard decision: 45 calendar days. Expedited: 72 hours. No cost to the member."

A Gold plan member needs residential mental health treatment for 30 days. What approvals are needed and what are the coverage limits?,"Residential mental health treatment is covered under the Gold plan up to 60 days per plan year, so a 30-day stay falls within the annual limit. Prior authorization is required for residential treatment programs exceeding 14 consecutive days, so for a 30-day stay the member/provider would need to obtain prior authorization to cover the days beyond day 14. Inpatient behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment is covered at the same coinsurance rate as medical/surgical inpatient stays, consistent with the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act — for the Gold 80 plan, that means the $350/day inpatient copay for the first five days followed by 20% coinsurance for each additional day.","Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Services. Outpatient therapy sessions are covered at the specialist copay rate. Inpatient behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment is covered at the same coinsurance rate as medical/surgical inpatient stays, consistent with the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act. Prior authorization is required for residential treatment programs exceeding 14 consecutive days. <>
